A Little Background

Currently, I'm employed as a firearm designer(Believe it or don't idgaf. Can't say much more so take it with a grain of salt), but previously I made my money as a composite technician. I manufactured helicopter blades by hand and know a thing or two about composites. There were some improvements that would be easily doable for most making the armor in the video.

Issues

My primary issue with his assembly is that he used a non-isotropic layup. Okay, big words. What it mean doe?

Isotropic more or less means "The same in every direction". This relates to composites in how they bear loads. Solid metals bear loads isotropically because they are solid and have no gaps. They are capable of transferring forces in all directions.

A fabric cannot do this. Because a fabric weave is like this, it can only bear loads in the same directions as the fibers. This is called tensile strength. A measure of the tension the fibers can take before they snap. Here's what his schedule was like. This leaves a lot of gaps and makes the final product weaker. Think of the directions the fibers lead like an angle. 0 deg, 90 deg.

This is the way it should be done. Making your layup in this manner will leave less space between fibers for matrix, or resin, and will allow a more uniform distribution of applied forces. Both of these factors will help make your fiber to resin ratio closer to ideal and will make the overall laminate stronger.

One last thing he could have done would have been to use something like this, a 12 ton press, to evenly apply huge force to his laminate. If he placed those plates in a press between two pieces of plywood, he would have gotten a SUPER STRONG laminate with an impressive fiber to resin ratio. The finish would have looked like glass. It's likely that the cure would be semi-transparent. Especially if he left it in front of that space heater to cure.

Conclusion

Eh that's just my two cents. I would love to hear from anyone else on the subject. Armor seems pretty easy to make tbqh. Might try at some point myself.
